items.name: Earth from Orbit 2013
items.content: A highlight reel of some of the best images and data visualizations of the planet in 2013 from NASA and partner agency satellites.

items.name: Earth from Orbit 2014
items.content: Every day of every year, NASA satellites provide useful data about our home planet, and along the way, some beautiful images as well. This video includes satellite images of Earth in 2014 from NASA and its partners as well as photos and a time lapse video from the International Space Station. We’ve also included a range of data visualizations, model runs, and a conceptual animation that were produced in 2014 (but in some cases might have been utilizing data from earlier years.) Below is a full list of the images included.

items.name: Earth from Orbit 2019: How NASA Satellites #PictureEarth
items.content: This Earth Day, NASA invites you to share how you #PictureEarth. For inspiration, NASA collected some of the best and most inconic satellite images and data visualizations capture over the last year. NASA's space-based view of our planet, and the way it's changing, helps humans understand Earth better.

items.name: Goodnight Earth
items.content: The Artemis II crew captures the exact moment of Earth set from windows on the Orion capsule, on the sixth day of their mission, as they fly behind the Moon. In the background, Commander Reid Wiseman can be heard commenting, “Dude. No way.”

items.name: NASA’s Perseverance Rover Microphone Captures Sounds from Mars - B
items.content: This set of sounds from the surface of Mars were recorded by the microphone on the side of NASA’s Perseverance Rover on February 20, 2021. In the first set, sounds from the rover itself dominate. In the second set, the sound was filtered to make sounds from Mars more audible. You can hear a little wind in the second set. This is the first time a Mars rover has been equipped with a microphone. The images in this video were taken by Perseverance's Navigation Cameras, or Navcams, on the same day as the microphone sounds, February 20, 2021. For more information about Perseverance, visit https://mars.nasa.gov/perseverance Credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech

items.name: Space 24/7/365: Space Station Benefits
items.content: As a home to humans and a lab for scientific research for more than 20 years, the International Space Station is a one-of-a-kind platform for advancing technologies such as robots, computers, health monitors, life support systems, and more for both space and ground applications. The station also has made it possible for numerous experiments to delve into how space travel affects people physically and psychologically – knowledge that often improves the quality of life for people on Earth, too. Learn more: https://go.nasa.gov/4cplI8V Explore other station benefits: https://www.nasa.gov/stationbenefits Image Credit: Canadian Space Agency 0:17

items.name: Sleep for Health
items.content: Told from the viewpoint of a child, this film emphasizes that children should train themselves in good sleeping habits. In typical "Goofus and Gallant" style, it shows the advantages a well-rested kid has over his poor-sleeping classmate. Dreams are presented as a normal part of sleeping, and there is a funny dream sequence.
